q: Walk me through the patient journey in Health Cloud from start to finish.
alt: Explain the patient lifecycle in Health Cloud end to end.
What are the stages of patient care in Health Cloud and which objects are used at each?
Take me through how a patient moves through Health Cloud, from referral to follow-up.
patient journey health cloud walk through
a: I usually tell it as one patient's story. Say Maria is referred to a clinic for diabetes. The referral comes in as a Clinical Service Request, or she starts as a lead from a web form and gets converted. She becomes a person account, with her medical record number stored on the Identifier object, and we record her consent. Then we link her household and caregiver and set up her care team. The care manager runs an assessment, and the answers suggest problems and goals for a care plan built from a template. Appointments are booked through Intelligent Appointment Management. Her conditions, labs and medications flow in from the EHR into the FHIR-aligned clinical data model, usually through MuleSoft. The team monitors her on the timeline and through care gaps. When she's discharged after a hospital stay, the encounter update triggers follow-up tasks. Consent and privacy controls run across every stage.
points: Intake: referral (ClinicalServiceRequest) or lead conversion
Patient = person account + Identifier, consent, household, care team
Assessment -> care plan from template (Integrated Care Management)
Appointments, EHR clinical data, timeline and care gaps
Discharge (ClinicalEncounter) -> follow-up; consent and security throughout

q: How do you onboard a new patient or member in Health Cloud?
alt: What happens when a new patient is registered in Health Cloud?
Explain patient intake and onboarding in Health Cloud.
How is a patient record created and set up in Health Cloud?
new patient registration health cloud
a: Onboarding means creating one clean patient record and putting the basics around it. Say a new patient calls a clinic to register. The intake user first searches for an existing record, because duplicates are the biggest headache later. If none exists, they create a person account with the patient record type, and store identifiers like the medical record number or member ID on the Identifier object, linked to the account. Next comes consent, like the privacy notice or consent to join a program, then household and caregiver relationships, and the care team. Many orgs wrap all of this in one guided OmniScript so the front desk can't skip a step. Person accounts are the recommended model because a patient is an individual, and a caregiver who later becomes a patient doesn't need remodeling.
points: Search first to avoid duplicates
Person account for the patient, Identifier for MRN or member ID
Capture consent, household, caregiver and care team
Often wrapped in a guided OmniScript

q: How do you convert a lead into a patient in Health Cloud?
alt: What is lead to patient conversion in Health Cloud?
How does Convert to Patient work?
A prospective patient is a lead. How does it become a patient record?
lead conversion person account health cloud
a: Health Cloud lets you capture a prospective patient as a lead and convert it into a patient, and the result is always a person account. Say a clinic runs a weight-management campaign and people fill in a web form. They land as leads and an intake coordinator qualifies them. Health Cloud adds patient fields to the lead, like a medical record number, and the Individual Record Type Mapper decides which lead record types convert to patients. The coordinator uses the Convert to Patient action, which comes from the HealthCloudExtensions package, or you build your own process in Flow. Before converting, the process compares the source system ID and medical record number with existing accounts and flags a match as a duplicate instead of creating a second patient. The gotcha is field mapping: custom lead fields must be mapped to account or contact, or that data is lost at conversion.
points: Result is always a person account
Individual Record Type Mapper routes lead record types
Convert to Patient (HealthCloudExtensions) or a custom Flow
Duplicate check on source system ID and MRN
Map custom lead fields before converting

q: How do assessments work in Health Cloud?
alt: What are Health Cloud assessments and how are they built?
Explain Discovery Framework assessments in Health Cloud.
How do you create a screening questionnaire for patients in Health Cloud?
assessments vs surveys in health cloud
a: Assessments are structured questionnaires, like a fall-risk or depression screening, built on Discovery Framework with OmniStudio. Say a care manager screens every new patient for fall risk. An admin creates assessment questions and question sets in the OmniStudio app, then clicks Build OmniScript, which generates a Discovery Framework OmniScript. Once activated, it can sit on the patient page or an Experience Cloud site. Answers are stored in Discovery Framework objects such as Assessment and AssessmentQuestionResponse, so they're reportable. The useful part for care management is that admins can map responses to recommendations, so a high-risk answer suggests a problem, goal or intervention when the care manager builds the care plan. That mapping uses the AsmtQstnRespRecommendation object with a decision table. I'd also mention that assessments are not the same as Salesforce Surveys; surveys suit simple feedback, assessments suit clinical screening.
points: Built with Discovery Framework + OmniStudio (Build OmniScript)
Objects: Assessment, AssessmentQuestion, AssessmentQuestionSet, AssessmentQuestionResponse
Responses can drive care plan recommendations (AsmtQstnRespRecommendation + decision table)
Different from Salesforce Surveys

q: What is the PGI library in Health Cloud?
alt: What does Problem Goal Intervention library mean?
What are ProblemDefinition and GoalDefinition used for?
How are care plan templates built in Integrated Care Management?
p g i library health cloud
a: The PGI library is the reusable catalog of Problems, Goals and Interventions that care plan templates are built from. Say a clinic manages heart failure patients. An admin creates a ProblemDefinition for heart failure, GoalDefinition records like 'weight stays within target', and action plan templates for interventions like weekly nurse calls. ProblemGoalDefinition links problems to goals, since one goal can serve many problems. A CarePlanTemplate then arranges these into a structure. When a care manager creates a plan for a real patient, the definitions turn into records on that patient: problems become HealthCondition records and goals become GoalAssignment records. The value is consistency. Every nurse uses the same wording and the same interventions, and reporting across patients works because everything points at the same definitions.
points: ProblemDefinition, GoalDefinition, ProblemGoalDefinition junction
Interventions come from action plan templates
CarePlanTemplate arranges the PGI items
Instantiated as HealthCondition and GoalAssignment on the patient

q: Walk me through the life of a care plan in Health Cloud, from creation to closure.
alt: How is a care plan created, tracked and closed in Health Cloud?
What happens to a care plan after it is created?
Explain the care plan lifecycle in Integrated Care Management.
care plan life cycle health cloud
a: A care plan goes from template, to an active plan on the patient, to review and closure. Say a patient is diagnosed with COPD. The care manager opens the care plan FlexCard on the patient's person account and clicks New Care Plan, which runs an OmniScript. They pick the COPD template, and the assessment results suggest extra problems or goals, like quitting smoking. The plan is saved as a CarePlan record, goals become GoalAssignment records, and interventions from action plan templates become tasks for the team. Over the next weeks the team completes tasks, records outcomes and updates goal progress, while CRM Analytics dashboards show plan status and overdue tasks. When the goals are met, the plan status is set to Completed, or Cancelled if the patient leaves the program, and its history stays visible. One thing to watch: older orgs may still use the managed-package care plan, which was a Case.
points: Create: New Care Plan on the FlexCard runs an OmniScript with a template
CarePlan, GoalAssignment, interventions as tasks
Track progress, outcomes, dashboards
Close: status Completed or Cancelled; legacy orgs use Case-based care plans

q: What are care gaps in Health Cloud and how do they get closed?
alt: Explain care gaps and clinical measures in Health Cloud.
How does Health Cloud find missing preventive care?
What is a CareGap record?
care gap closure process
a: A care gap is a recommended service a patient should have had but hasn't, like a diabetic patient with no eye exam in the last year. In Health Cloud the rule is defined as a ClinicalMeasure with its criteria. A care manager clicks New Care Gap on the care gap FlexCard, which runs an OmniScript that evaluates the measure against the patient's data, and if the measure isn't met, a CareGap record is created. Gaps can also be imported from a quality or analytics system, or entered manually. From the gap, the care manager can create a care plan or arrange the missing service. Once the eye exam happens and the data comes in, re-evaluating the measure closes the gap. Payers care a lot about this because closed gaps drive quality scores, so I'd also report on open gaps by provider or program.
points: ClinicalMeasure + criteria define the rule
CareGap created by evaluation, import or manual entry
Care plans can be created from care gaps
Re-evaluation after the service closes the gap

q: What is the difference between a ClinicalEncounter and an appointment in Health Cloud?
alt: Encounter vs appointment in Health Cloud, when is each used?
Is a visit stored as ClinicalEncounter or ServiceAppointment?
How do you model visits and hospital stays in Health Cloud?
clinical encounter versus service appointment
a: A ClinicalEncounter is the clinical record of a visit or stay that happened or is happening, while an appointment is the scheduling record for a planned time slot. Say a patient books a cardiology visit for Tuesday at 10. That booking is a ServiceAppointment when scheduling runs on Salesforce Scheduler or Field Service, or a slot in the EHR's schedule. On Tuesday the EHR records the actual visit, and it comes into Health Cloud as a ClinicalEncounter with a status like In Progress or Finished, start and end dates, the facility, and related diagnosis and provider records. Encounters also cover hospital stays, with an admission source and a discharge disposition. So I use appointments for access, booking and no-show reporting, and encounters for clinical history and follow-up logic like 'discharged yesterday'.
points: Appointment = planned slot (ServiceAppointment or EHR schedule)
ClinicalEncounter = actual visit or stay, FHIR Encounter aligned
Encounter has Status, StartDate, EndDate, FacilityId, DischargeDispositionId
Child objects: ClinicalEncounterDiagnosis, ClinicalEncounterProvider

q: How does consent management work in Health Cloud?
alt: Which objects store patient consent in Health Cloud?
How do you capture and track a signed consent form?
Explain Authorization Form and Data Use Purpose.
patient consent tracking health cloud
a: Health Cloud consent management tracks which document a patient agreed to, for which purpose, and how. Say a hospital runs a remote monitoring program that needs a signed data-sharing consent. An admin creates a Data Use Purpose for the program, an Authorization Form with its revision and effective dates, and Authorization Form Text that holds the actual document, one per language if needed. Authorization Form Data Use links the form to the purpose. When the patient signs on the portal or in person, an Authorization Form Consent record captures who gave consent, the method and the status. So months later anyone can see exactly which version she signed and when. Communication preferences, like opting out of marketing texts, sit separately in the standard ContactPointTypeConsent model, so I don't mix clinical consent with marketing opt-outs.
points: DataUsePurpose, AuthorizationForm, AuthorizationFormText, AuthorizationFormDataUse
AuthorizationFormConsent records each consent: giver, method, status
Versioned text per language or region
Communication opt-outs: ContactPointTypeConsent

q: Walk me through the member lifecycle for a health plan in Health Cloud.
alt: How does a payer use Health Cloud across the member journey?
Explain the payer side lifecycle, from enrollment to care management.
What objects does a health insurer use for members in Health Cloud?
member journey payer health cloud
a: For a payer, the lifecycle follows the member rather than a single visit. Say a health plan signs a new employer group. Group quoting and enrollment set up the purchaser's plan, and each person gets a MemberPlan linking them to the PurchaserPlan with their coverage. The member's person account then becomes the hub for service: contact center agents see the member 360 with benefits, coverage and claims data from the core claims system. When a doctor requests an MRI, Utilization Management handles the prior authorization as a Care Request. If the member has a chronic condition, they're enrolled in a care management program and get a care plan, and care gaps flag missed preventive care. Provider network management keeps the directory current and referrals in network. Appeals, grievances and renewals close the loop. I always confirm which of these the payer runs in Salesforce and which stay in their core admin platform.
points: Enrollment: PurchaserPlan, MemberPlan, coverage benefits
Member service: member 360, benefits and claims visibility
Utilization Management: Care Request for prior authorization
Care management programs, care plans, care gaps
Provider network, appeals and grievances

q: Health Cloud is now called Agentforce Health. What does that change?
alt: What is Agentforce Health?
Is Health Cloud renamed?
Agentforce Health vs Health Cloud, are they different products?
agent force health formerly health cloud
a: It's mainly a rebrand: Salesforce now markets the product as Agentforce Health (formerly Health Cloud), in line with putting Agentforce across its industry clouds. Underneath it's the same platform: person account patients, the clinical data model, Integrated Care Management, Utilization Management, provider management and so on. Say a client's RFP asks for Agentforce Health experience: that's Health Cloud experience. What changed is the emphasis on AI agents that work on that data, like agents that verify benefits or help schedule appointments. The developer guide is now titled the Agentforce Health Developer Guide, but objects like HealthCondition and CarePlan keep their names, and many setup screens still say Health Cloud. Life Sciences Cloud got the same treatment and is now Agentforce Life Sciences. In an interview I mention both names, which shows I'm current without confusing anyone.
points: Agentforce Health = Health Cloud, rebranded
Same data model and features; object names unchanged
Bigger focus on AI agents on top of health data
Life Sciences Cloud is now Agentforce Life Sciences

q: What is Agentforce for Health and what can its agents do?
alt: What AI agent capabilities does Salesforce offer for healthcare?
Give examples of Agentforce use cases in Health Cloud.
How is Agentforce used by providers and payers?
agentforce for health skills and actions
a: Agentforce for Health is a library of prebuilt agent skills and actions for healthcare, built on Health Cloud and Life Sciences Cloud data, released in February 2025. Examples: provider search and scheduling, where an agent matches a patient to an in-network provider and books a visit; care coordination, like pre-visit summaries and eligibility or prior authorization checks with payers through partner networks; benefits verification for pharmacy and equipment benefits; disease surveillance for public health, turning lab reports into cases; and home health documentation support. Say a patient messages a clinic at night asking for a dermatologist: an agent can find in-network options, offer slots, and hand off to a human if it gets clinical. When I talk about it, I stress guardrails: identity verification, grounding only on that patient's data, the Einstein Trust Layer, and checking that the BAA covers the AI services being used.
points: Prebuilt healthcare agent skills and actions
Provider search and scheduling, care coordination, benefits verification
Public health disease surveillance, home health
Guardrails: identity, grounding, Trust Layer, BAA coverage

q: What is the difference between Health Cloud and Life Sciences Cloud?
alt: Health Cloud vs Life Sciences Cloud, who uses which?
When would a company choose Life Sciences Cloud instead of Health Cloud?
Is Life Sciences Cloud part of Health Cloud?
agentforce life sciences vs agentforce health
a: Health Cloud is for providers and payers, while Life Sciences Cloud, now Agentforce Life Sciences, is for pharma, biotech and medtech companies. Say a hospital wants care plans for its heart patients: that's Health Cloud. A drug maker wants a patient support program for a specialty medicine, needs to recruit clinical trial participants, or manages reps' meetings with doctors: that's Life Sciences Cloud. Earlier, life sciences companies often used Health Cloud for patient programs, which is why you still see overlap in things like care programs. Salesforce then built Life Sciences Cloud as its own product, launched around 2024, with clinical trial and customer engagement features. In an interview I'd say the first question is who the customer is, provider, payer or manufacturer, because that decides the product and the licenses.
points: Health Cloud (Agentforce Health): providers and payers
Life Sciences Cloud (Agentforce Life Sciences): pharma, biotech, medtech
Life sciences: patient services, clinical trials, HCP engagement
Customer type decides the product

q: What role does OmniStudio play in Health Cloud?
alt: Why do Health Cloud projects need OmniStudio?
Where are FlexCards and OmniScripts used in Health Cloud?
Do I need to know OmniStudio for Health Cloud?
omni studio in health cloud
a: OmniStudio is the toolkit Health Cloud uses for most of its guided screens and compact data views. FlexCards show patient information, OmniScripts run step-by-step processes, Integration Procedures fetch and combine data, and Data Mappers (formerly DataRaptors) read, transform and save records. Say a care manager clicks New Care Plan: that launches an OmniScript, and the care plan view itself is a FlexCard. Assessments are Discovery Framework OmniScripts, patient self-scheduling uses the Intelligent Appointment Management OmniScripts, and Utilization Management uses Integration Procedures and Data Mappers to pull member data from the EHR. So on a Health Cloud project I need to read and customize these, not just build Flows. My habit is to copy or version the shipped OmniScripts before changing them, so later upgrades don't wipe my work.
points: FlexCards, OmniScripts, Integration Procedures, Data Mappers (formerly DataRaptors)
Care plans, care gaps, assessments, scheduling all use OmniStudio
Customize copies or new versions of shipped components

q: What are CodeSet and CodeSetBundle in Health Cloud, and why are they needed?
alt: How are medical codes like ICD-10 or SNOMED stored in Health Cloud?
Why does HealthCondition point to a CodeSetBundle?
Explain code sets in the clinical data model.
code set bundle health cloud
a: CodeSet stores a single code from a coding system, and CodeSetBundle groups equivalent codes from different systems, so one clinical concept is referenced once. Say a patient has type 2 diabetes. The EHR might send an ICD-10 code, while the problem list uses SNOMED. Each code is a CodeSet record, and a CodeSetBundle groups them as the same concept. Clinical records point to the bundle; for example HealthCondition.ConditionCodeId is a required lookup to CodeSetBundle, and MedicationStatement can point to CodeSetBundle through MedicationCodeId, or to a Medication record instead. The benefit is that queries and reports work on one concept regardless of which coding system the source used. The gotcha on projects is load order: code sets must be loaded before the clinical data, or inserts fail because the code lookup is required.
points: CodeSet = one code (ICD-10, SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm)
CodeSetBundle = group of equivalent codes
HealthCondition.ConditionCodeId -> CodeSetBundle (required)
Load code sets before clinical data

q: What is the difference between the Health Cloud managed package and the standard Health Cloud objects?
alt: HealthCloudGA package objects vs standard objects, what changed?
Why do some Health Cloud orgs have custom EHR objects?
Old Health Cloud data model vs new data model.
managed package versus core objects health cloud
a: Health Cloud started as a managed package with custom objects in the HealthCloudGA namespace, and over time Salesforce moved most of the data model to standard platform objects. Say you join a project on an org set up several years ago: you may find the older EHR custom objects from the package, care plans built as Case records, and the older timeline. A newer org uses standard objects like HealthCondition, CareObservation and CarePlan, Integrated Care Management, and the Enhanced Timeline. Both can exist in the same org, since the package may still be installed for some features. For new work I build on the standard objects, because new features, FHIR mappings and Agentforce for Health target them. When an org is on the old model, I don't rip it out blindly; I plan a migration with data mapping and parallel testing.
points: Old: HealthCloudGA custom objects, Case-based care plans
New: standard FHIR-aligned objects, CarePlan, Enhanced Timeline
Both can coexist in one org
Build new work on standard objects; migrate deliberately

q: How does Provider Search work behind the scenes in Health Cloud?
alt: Why does a new doctor not show up in Provider Search?
What is CareProviderSearchableField?
How do you set up data for provider search?
provider search sync health cloud
a: Provider Search doesn't query the provider records directly; a sync process copies provider data into a flattened search object, CareProviderSearchableField, and the search component queries that. Say a care coordinator needs an orthopedic surgeon near the patient. Behind that search, practitioners and facilities are HealthcareProvider records linked to contacts and accounts, and HealthcarePractitionerFacility links each practitioner to every facility where they work. The provider sync fills the searchable object: the Data Processing Engine version runs once a day, the legacy version every six hours, and you can trigger it manually. If a newly added doctor doesn't show up, I check the Provider Search Sync Logs for failures, and that required fields like names and addresses are filled. You can also add custom fields, like languages spoken, to make them searchable.
points: Search runs on CareProviderSearchableField, filled by provider sync
Source: HealthcareProvider + HealthcarePractitionerFacility
DPE sync daily, legacy every six hours, manual trigger possible
Troubleshoot with Provider Search Sync Logs

q: What do you consider before using Shield Platform Encryption on patient data?
alt: Should we encrypt all PHI fields in Health Cloud?
Deterministic vs probabilistic encryption for patient data.
What breaks when you turn on Platform Encryption?
shield encryption health cloud trade offs
a: Shield Platform Encryption protects PHI at rest, but every encrypted field has a cost, so I encrypt deliberately rather than everything. Say a clinic wants to encrypt date of birth, a national ID number and clinical notes. With probabilistic encryption you can't filter or sort on the field in SOQL, list views or reports, which breaks things like finding a patient by date of birth. Deterministic encryption allows exact-match filtering, so I use it for fields people search on. Encryption also limits some formulas, report features and matching rules, so I retest automation and integrations after enabling it. I check which standard Health Cloud fields support encryption and plan key management, like tenant secret rotation and Bring Your Own Key if required. And encryption isn't access control: a user with read access still sees the decrypted value, so sharing and field-level security still matter.
points: Probabilistic: strongest, but no filtering or sorting
Deterministic: allows exact-match filtering
Retest formulas, reports, duplicate rules, integrations
Key management: rotation, BYOK
Encryption is not access control

q: What is the difference between field history tracking, Field Audit Trail and Event Monitoring for patient data?
alt: How do you audit changes vs views of patient records?
Field Audit Trail vs Event Monitoring, which one do I need for HIPAA?
Can field history show who looked at a patient record?
audit options for phi in salesforce
a: They answer different audit questions. Field history tracking records who changed a field and when, for a limited number of fields and a limited time. Field Audit Trail, part of Shield, extends change history to more fields and keeps it for years, which suits medical record retention rules. Event Monitoring records activity, like who viewed a record, ran or exported a report, called the API, or logged in. Say a patient complains that her allergy list was changed and that someone looked at her chart without reason. The allergy change shows in field history or Field Audit Trail; the chart view shows in Event Monitoring, for example in LightningUriEvent records. So for a HIPAA access audit, history tracking alone isn't enough, because reading a record isn't a change.
points: Field history: up to 20 fields per object, about 18 months in the UI (24 via API)
Field Audit Trail: up to 60 fields, retention up to 10 years
Event Monitoring: views, reports, exports, API, logins
Access audits need Event Monitoring

q: Write Apex to create a patient as a person account and store the MRN in Health Cloud.
alt: How do you insert a person account patient with Apex?
Create a Health Cloud patient and its medical record number in code.
Apex example for patient registration in Health Cloud.
insert person account apex identifier
a: I create the patient as an Account with a person account record type, and Salesforce turns it into a person account with its contact behind it. Say a registration portal sends new patients to Salesforce. I get the record type by developer name, never a hard-coded Id, set person fields like FirstName, LastName, PersonBirthdate and PersonEmail, and insert in bulk. Then I store the medical record number on the Identifier object with ParentRecordId pointing to the new account, because a patient can have several IDs from different systems. In a real build I'd check for an existing patient by MRN before inserting, and use user mode so the caller's permissions apply.
points: Person account = Account with a person account record type
Record type by developer name, no hard-coded Ids
MRN goes on Identifier (ParentRecordId, IdValue)
Bulk inserts, user mode, duplicate check first

q: Write a query to get a patient's active conditions and allergies in Health Cloud.
alt: SOQL on HealthCondition and AllergyIntolerance for one patient.
How do you fetch problems and allergies for an LWC on the patient page?
Query active diagnoses and allergies by patient.
soql health condition allergy intolerance
a: I query HealthCondition and AllergyIntolerance by PatientId, which is the master-detail to the patient's account, and get the code name through the code lookup. Say a nurse opens a patient before a procedure and needs active problems and allergies on one card. For conditions I filter on ConditionStatus, and for allergies on Status. The code names come from CodeSetBundle through the ConditionCode and Code relationships. WITH USER_MODE makes sure the nurse's own field-level security and sharing apply, which matters for PHI. Picklist API values can differ from labels, so I check them in the org before hard-coding filters.
points: Both objects link to the patient via PatientId (master-detail to Account)
Code names via CodeSetBundle lookups
WITH USER_MODE for PHI
Verify picklist API values

q: Write Apex to share a patient record with the assigned nurse in a Private sharing model.
alt: How do you share a person account with a user in Apex?
Apex sharing for Health Cloud patients, how?
Create AccountShare records for nurses assigned to patients.
apex managed sharing person account
a: For a person account patient I share the Account, because the person's contact and master-detail clinical records like HealthCondition follow the account's access. Say each nurse should see the patients on her custom Assigned Nurse field. On a standard object like Account you can't create custom Apex sharing reasons, so I insert AccountShare rows, which get the Manual row cause, in bulk from the trigger handler. I give Read on the account and None on opportunities and cases unless the nurse needs them. The gotchas: manual shares are removed when the record owner changes, so I re-run the logic on owner change, and I delete the old share when the assigned nurse changes. Objects that aren't master-detail to the patient need their own sharing.
points: Share the Account; master-detail children follow
No custom Apex sharing reasons on standard objects: Manual row cause
Manual shares drop on owner change: re-run logic
Remove old shares when assignment changes

q: Write Apex to find who viewed a specific patient's record using Event Monitoring.
alt: How do you query LightningUriEvent for record views?
A privacy officer asks who opened a patient chart last week. How do you get it?
SOQL on real-time event monitoring for patient access audit.
lightning uri event query apex
a: With Shield or the Event Monitoring add-on, Real-Time Event Monitoring stores Lightning record views in LightningUriEvent, and I can query it. Say a privacy officer asks who opened a VIP patient's record in the last week. LightningUriEvent has EventDate, Username, RecordId and Operation, which is exactly what she needs, but its SOQL is restricted: you can filter only on EventDate and EventIdentifier, and ORDER BY only supports EventDate descending. So I filter by date in SOQL and match the RecordId in Apex. Event storage must be enabled for that event, and the user needs the View Real-Time Event Monitoring Data permission. This covers Lightning Experience views; API reads appear in ApiEvent and report runs in ReportEvent, so a full audit checks those too.
points: LightningUriEvent: EventDate, Username, RecordId, Operation
Filter only on EventDate or EventIdentifier; match RecordId in Apex
Needs Shield or Event Monitoring + View Real-Time Event Monitoring Data
Also check ApiEvent and ReportEvent

q: Write a scheduled Apex job that creates follow-up tasks for patients discharged yesterday.
alt: How do you query discharged encounters and create tasks in Apex?
Automate post-discharge follow-up calls with Apex.
Schedulable class on ClinicalEncounter example.
discharge follow up task apex
a: I find encounters that finished yesterday and create one follow-up task per patient for the patient's owner, usually the care coordinator. Say a hospital wants a call within 48 hours of every discharge. A scheduled job runs each morning, queries ClinicalEncounter for status Finished and an EndDate of yesterday, and inserts tasks due tomorrow. Before inserting, it checks for an open follow-up task so a rerun doesn't create duplicates. In a real build I'd also exclude dispositions like transfer to hospice using DischargeDispositionId, switch to Batch Apex if volumes are large, and if the EHR sends discharges in near real time, a record-triggered flow on the encounter is simpler than a nightly job.
points: ClinicalEncounter: Status Finished + EndDate = YESTERDAY
One task per patient, owned by the patient owner
Skip patients with an open follow-up task
Consider DischargeDispositionId exclusions and Batch Apex for volume

q: A clinic wants nurses to see only their own patients. How would you set it up?
alt: Nurses should not see patients assigned to other nurses. What do you do?
How do you restrict patient visibility to the assigned nurse?
Each nurse has a panel of patients and should only see those. How?
nurse sees only own patients health cloud
a: I'd make patient records private and then open access only to the assigned nurse. Say a clinic has twelve nurses, each with a panel of patients. Step one, set the Account org-wide default to Private; person accounts already require Contact to be controlled by parent, so the contact side follows. Step two, define what 'own patient' means: the nurse owns the patient record, or there's an assigned nurse field or a care team membership. If the nurse is the owner, Private is enough. If not, automation shares the record with the nurse when she's assigned and removes it when she isn't. Step three, clinical records with a master-detail to the patient follow automatically, but any object with its own sharing needs the same treatment. Step four, make sure nurse permission sets don't have View All, and test by logging in as two different nurses.
points: Account OWD Private
Define ownership or assignment, share via automation
Master-detail clinical records follow the patient
No View All in nurse permission sets; test with login as

q: A hospital sends referrals that must automatically create the patient and start a care plan. How would you design it?
alt: Referral from a hospital must create a patient and a care plan. Walk me through it.
How would you automate referral intake to care plan in Health Cloud?
Inbound referral should create the patient if new and kick off care management. Design it.
referral to patient and care plan automation
a: I'd break it into intake, patient matching, acceptance, then the care plan. Say a hospital refers a heart failure patient to a cardiology practice. First, intake: if the referral arrives over FHIR or HL7, MuleSoft maps it to a ClinicalServiceRequest; if it comes by fax, Intelligent Document Automation extracts it from a Received Document. Second, matching: search the Identifier for the MRN, then name plus date of birth; if there's no match, create a person account, and if the match is weak, send it to a review queue rather than guess. Third, an intake coordinator accepts the referral using the IsAccepted field on the Clinical Service Request. Fourth, a flow assigns a care manager and creates a task, and the care manager uses New Care Plan with the heart failure template. I keep that last step human because the plan needs clinical judgement, while everything before it is automated.
points: Intake: FHIR/HL7 via MuleSoft or fax via Intelligent Document Automation
Match on Identifier (MRN), then demographics; weak matches to review
Accept referral (IsAccepted on ClinicalServiceRequest)
Assign care manager; care plan from template

q: You need to sync allergies from the EHR into Health Cloud. How would you do it?
alt: How would you bring allergy data from Epic into Salesforce?
Design an integration for AllergyIntolerance from the EHR.
The nurses want EHR allergies visible in the patient 360. Steps?
sync allergies ehr fhir health cloud

q: A hospital wants a follow-up call within 48 hours after every discharge. How would you set it up?

Automate post-discharge outreach in Health Cloud.

transition of care follow up call
a: I'd trigger a follow-up task from the encounter that marks the discharge. Say a patient goes home after pneumonia on Monday. A record-triggered flow on ClinicalEncounter fires when the status changes to Finished, checks the disposition to skip cases like death or transfer to another hospital, and creates a task for the patient's care coordinator due within two days. If the task is still open after a day, an escalation alerts the team lead. The call itself can follow a short OmniScript covering medications, symptoms and whether a follow-up visit is booked. Finally, a report shows the percentage of discharges called within 48 hours, which is what the hospital will measure.

q: Patients send blood pressure readings from home devices. The care coordinator must be alerted when a reading is too high. How would you build it?

rpm blood pressure alert care observation

Step two, thresholds: a program default, plus a patient-specific target from the care plan goal. Step three, evaluate asynchronously, in the integration layer or an async path of a record-triggered flow, so loading isn't slowed down. Step four, for a high reading, create one task or custom notification for the coordinator, but only if there's no open alert for that patient already. Step five, show the trend on the timeline or a FlexCard chart so the coordinator sees context, not one number.

Step four, rebuild pages, Enhanced Timeline definitions, reports and sharing. Step five, run both in parallel, reconcile counts per patient, then retire the old objects. Clinician sign-off on sample patients is my go-live gate.

q: A clinic wants an Agentforce agent on its patient portal that can reschedule appointments. How would you design it safely?

agentforce patient portal appointment agent

a: Real PHI shouldn't sit in sandboxes where developers and vendors work, so I'd mask it or use synthetic data. Say a health system refreshes a full sandbox for user testing. Step four, document all of this, because auditors will ask how PHI is protected outside production.

q: A portal patient reports she can see another patient's appointment. What do you do?

Data leak on the patient portal, how would you troubleshoot it?
What usually causes portal users to see other users' records?
patient portal privacy breach troubleshooting
a: I treat it as a possible privacy breach first and a bug second. Say a patient emails the clinic a screenshot of someone else's upcoming visit. Step one, contain: involve the privacy officer, and if the cause isn't obvious, disable the affected component or page right away. Step two, find the cause, usually one of a few: a sharing set mapping the wrong field, like a household account instead of the patient's own account; external org-wide defaults set to Public Read; a guest user with record access; or Apex behind an LWC running without sharing or without user mode. Step three, fix it and test with two test patient users side by side. Step four, use Event Monitoring data to see who viewed what during the exposure window, because compliance needs that to decide whether breach notification is required. Step five, add a regression test so it can't come back.

q: A care coordinator wants to record that a patient has no transport to appointments and do something about it. How would you set it up?
alt: How are social determinants of health captured in Health Cloud?
Track SDOH barriers like housing or food insecurity.
Patient keeps missing visits because of transport. How does Health Cloud help?
sdoh care barrier health cloud
a: I'd capture it as a social determinant of health and turn it into an action on the care plan. Say a diabetic patient keeps missing visits because she has no car. Health Cloud has objects for this: CareDeterminantType holds the standard list, grouped into domains like transportation, food and housing, and the care barrier objects record that this specific patient has the barrier. In practice the coordinator finds it through an assessment question like 'Do you have reliable transport to appointments?', and the answer records a transportation barrier. The care plan then gets an intervention, like arranging a ride service or moving some visits to telehealth. The care plan FlexCard shows social determinants next to clinical problems, so the whole team sees them. Reporting across patients shows how many have transport barriers, which helps the clinic justify a ride program.
points: CareDeterminantType: standard determinants by domain
Care barrier objects record the patient-specific barrier
Found via assessment; addressed by interventions
Visible on the care plan FlexCard; reportable

q: A clinic gets hundreds of faxed referrals a week and staff retype them. How would you automate it?
alt: Automate fax referral intake in Health Cloud.
What is Intelligent Document Automation used for?
How do you turn incoming documents into referrals?
fax referral ocr health cloud
a: I'd use Intelligent Document Automation to turn faxes into referrals, with a person checking the result. Say a specialty clinic receives referral faxes from family doctors. Inbound faxes and emails land as Received Document records. I create two queues, one for new documents and one for processed ones. A record-triggered flow puts new documents in the first queue. A second flow, triggered when the document's OCR status shows the text is extracted, moves it to the processed queue and calls the Process Received Document action, on a Run Asynchronously path so a failure doesn't break the save. That action reads the patient details and the requested service and creates a Clinical Service Request. Intake staff then review it, fix anything misread, and accept the referral using the IsAccepted field. The typing goes away, but the human check stays.
points: Received Document holds the inbound fax and extracted text
Queues + record-triggered flows on OcrStatus
Process Received Document action creates a Clinical Service Request
Run asynchronously; human review and IsAccepted

q: A nurse care coordinator leaves the organization. What do you do with her patients and her work?
alt: A care team member resigns. How do you reassign patients and tasks?
Steps to offboard a clinical user in Health Cloud.
How do you hand over a coordinator's caseload?
user leaves reassign patients health cloud
a: I'd freeze her user, move her work to the right people, then deactivate. Say a coordinator managing about 150 patients leaves on Friday. Step one, freeze the user so she can't log in, without breaking ownership yet. Step two, reassign the patient records she owns, her care plans and her open tasks to the replacement coordinator or the team lead, using mass transfer or Data Loader. Step three, update care teams so she's removed and the new coordinator is added, because colleagues and portal patients look at the care team to know who to contact. Step four, check sharing: manual shares are dropped when the owner changes, so any access that depended on ownership must be recreated, and shares granted to her should be removed. Step five, check flows, queues and assignment rules that mention her, then deactivate. A report on open tasks by owner confirms nothing was left behind.
points: Freeze first, deactivate last
Transfer patients, care plans, open tasks
Update care team membership
Recreate sharing lost on owner change; fix automation references
